classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate radicand inequalities, endpoint shifts, reflections and dilation to determine domain, range and curve direction, checking less familiar forms with substituted points.

content.prompt: State the domain and range of these functions and sketch the function.

answer.worked: The radicand requires $x\geq0$, and the square root is non-negative. Start at $(0,0)$ and sketch through $(1,1)$ and $(4,2)$, continuing right and upwards.

spec.description: Increasing square-root curve with included endpoint at the origin.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}x-2&\geq0\\x&\geq2\end{aligned}$$

The square root is non-negative. Translate $y=\sqrt{x}$ two units right. Start at $(2,0)$ and pass through $(3,1)$ and $(6,2)$.

spec.description: Increasing curve translated two units right.

$$\begin{aligned}x+5&\geq0\\x&\geq-5\end{aligned}$$

The square root is non-negative. Translate $y=\sqrt{x}$ five units left. Start at $(-5,0)$ and pass through $(-4,1)$ and $(-1,2)$.

spec.description: Increasing curve translated five units left.

Since $\sqrt{x+5}\geq0$, $y\geq1$. Translate the basic curve five units left and one unit up. Start at $(-5,1)$ and pass through $(-4,2)$ and $(-1,3)$.

$$\begin{aligned}x+5&\geq0\\x&\geq-5\end{aligned}$$

Since $\sqrt{x+5}\geq0$, $y\geq-4$. Translate the basic curve five units left and four units down. Start at $(-5,-4)$ and pass through $(-4,-3)$ and $(-1,-2)$. The $x$-intercept is $(11,0)$.

spec.description: Increasing curve from (-5,-4), continuing through its x-intercept.

Since $-\sqrt{x+5}\leq0$, $y\leq-4$. Reflect the basic curve in the $x$-axis, then translate five units left and four units down. Start at $(-5,-4)$ and pass through $(-4,-5)$ and $(-1,-6)$, continuing right and downwards.

spec.description: Rightward decreasing curve with maximum y-value -4.
